L348@P15: 2.3. Rem~rks on Monsky and Washnitzer's ~ethod.
L349@P15: Their theory gives a p-adic cohomology theory, their cohomology
L350@P15: groups being modules over the ring W of Witt vectors of k.
L351@P15: According to their published work, they have only proven their
L352@P15: fundamental invariance assertion modulo torsion, i.e. after tensoring
L353@P15: by the quotient field K of W. However in a private communication,
L354@P15: as Grothendieck ~derstood it, Washnitzer indicated that they have
L355@P15: been able to remove this restriction. It is of course of essential
L356@P15: importance to have a theory with coefficients in W, rather than inK.

L358@P15: Their method semms too clo-sely bound to differential forms, which
L359@P15: practically limits its appli~ations to smooth schemes. For this reason
L360@P15: perhaps, they have so far not overcome certain technical difficulties,
L361@P15: and have been unable so far to prove some of the usual properties for
L362@P15: their cohomology : for example, that their cohomology groups are of
L363@P15: finite rank on W, even when X0 is projective on k.
L364@P15: Nevertheless, they have been able to utilize their theory to give
L365@P15: a form of the Lefschetz fixed point theorem, using completely continuous
L366@P15-16: operators, and, by applying this to the frobenius endomorphism of a 322
L367@P16: smooth scheme over a finite field, they prove the rationality of the
L368@P16: zeta function of this soheme (in a way similar to that of Dwork).
